project.name: AI Leverage Library
project.purpose: A Git-native, evidence-aware library of reproducible AI techniques organized by outcome rather than provider.
project.primaryUser: Practitioners and AI agents seeking reproducible, authority-bounded AI workflows
project.problemSolved: Useful AI workflows are commonly scattered across prompts, demonstrations, and tribal knowledge without reproducible verification or explicit human authority boundaries.
project.stage: 0.1.0 repository scaffold with one seed technique, tested experiment intake, and one accepted-with-limitations practitioner trial awaiting independent repetition; product use and organizational value are UNVERIFIED
project.deploymentTarget: UNVERIFIED - a static documentation site or PWA is specified, but no provider or deployment configuration exists

goals.statement: Maintain portable technique cards, catalogs, and evidence contracts that fail visibly when their structural claims drift.
Enable a practitioner or agent to find, apply, and verify an appropriate technique without hidden context.
Make technique publication and lifecycle promotion reproducible, reviewable, and resistant to evidence inflation.
Demonstrate that the library improves real AI-assisted work through retained outcome evidence.

journeys.name: Discover and apply a governed AI technique
journeys.trigger: A practitioner or AI agent has an outcome or problem suited to an AI-assisted workflow
journeys.actor: Practitioner or AI agent under human authority
journeys.action: Find a technique, supply required inputs, execute its workflow, and perform claim-matched verification
journeys.stateChange: An ad hoc AI attempt becomes a bounded, inspectable workflow result
journeys.authorityOrEvidence: Technique card, retained verification evidence, and required human review
journeys.nextState: Retain a result or experiment and reassess the technique's evidence status
journeys.outcome: A useful result whose limits and authority are explicit
missingProof: Independent repetition, real use, and measured outcome remain unverified

journeys.name: Author and publish a technique
missingProof: A retained example of a newly published technique completing the entire review workflow

journeys.name: Capture a candidate as a governed experiment
journeys.trigger: A promising prompt, correction, workflow, failure, reference, or research finding may contain a reusable technique
journeys.actor: Repository contributor or AI agent operating under retention authority
journeys.action: Preview a sanitized proposed experiment, review catalog overlap, explicitly authorize retention, and validate the resulting record
journeys.stateChange: An unstructured candidate becomes a traceable proposed experiment without claiming execution or outcome evidence
journeys.authorityOrEvidence: Sanitized source reference, retention authorization, validated experiment record, and human lifecycle gates
journeys.nextState: Retain an independent repetition or reject further validation with retained reasons
journeys.outcome: A structurally valid active experiment with an accepted-with-limitations practitioner result and explicit uncertainty and authority
missingProof: No independent repetition or observed user outcome has been retained

decisions.summary: Technique cards are canonical; catalogs are derived navigation.
Organize techniques by outcomes rather than vendors or models.
Evidence levels and human authority gates constrain lifecycle promotion.
Keep websites, skills, CLIs, and MCP servers as adapters over a portable content core.
The public repository grants no reuse license unless a separate license is added.
The capability horizon backlog is a non-authoritative option inventory; entries require explicit promotion before they become explorations, roadmap commitments, or canonical capabilities.
Experiment acquisition is preview-first, rejects raw prompt or source flags, and requires explicit retention authorization before writing a proposed record.

risks.summary: Technique value may remain a one-run documentation claim without independent repetition and observed outcomes.
evidence: One accepted-with-limitations practitioner result is retained, but it has no repetition, case study, or observed outcome

risks.summary: The seed card's evidence level may be mistaken for reproducibility after one accepted bounded trial.
evidence: content/techniques/discover/constraint-compilation.md remains experimental and concept; independent repetition is absent

risks.summary: Public visibility may be mistaken for permission to reuse despite the all-rights-reserved license.
An accepted practitioner artifact may be mistaken for a reproducible or observed user outcome.
evidence: The active experiment is accepted with retained protocol limitations and has not been repeated or observed in use

blockers.summary: No independent repetition proves the seed technique is reproducible under documented conditions.
evidence: EXP-20260915-001 retains one owner-accepted-with-limitations practitioner result; no second independent run or case study exists
blockers.resolutionCondition: Complete PROOF-002 with a second independent result, comparison, verification, and authorized human disposition.

proofEvents.name: Independent governed use of Constraint Compilation
proofEvents.whyItMatters: It is the smallest event that can distinguish a well-structured technique card from a technique that creates reproducible user value.
prerequisites: Name an authorized reviewer; the bounded searchable-documentation workflow is assigned
Retain the sanitized trial and procedural deviations
acceptanceCriteria: A practitioner who did not author the card follows the canonical workflow
Every compiled constraint traces to supplied evidence
The result preserves scope and authority boundaries
A human reviewer accepts or rejects the output against the documented contract

proofEvents.name: Independent repetition of Constraint Compilation
proofEvents.whyItMatters: PROOF-001 established one accepted-with-limitations bounded trial; repetition tests reproducibility rather than one-run plausibility.
prerequisites: Retain the PROOF-001 artifact and disposition
Use the proposed EXP-20260924-001 repetition protocol
Name a second practitioner whose non-authorship is verified
Preserve the stricter source-inspection boundary or approve deviations before execution
acceptanceCriteria: The second practitioner did not author the card
Every compiled constraint traces to supplied evidence
The result preserves scope and authority boundaries
Results and failures are compared with PROOF-001
An authorized human accepts or rejects the repetition

commercialEvidence.claim: The library improves the quality or speed of real AI-assisted work.

nextActions.action: Assign a second non-author practitioner and authorized reviewer to the validated EXP-20260924-001 protocol.
Run the repetition and retain its result, failures, comparison, and human disposition.
Reassess reproducibility and the seed technique status without automatic promotion.
